- issues opened in `story-repo`#11 ("Outline rev. 14: finite-pool check is consistent in pattern, not within ±0.02 per cell") by `idea-review-repo`  > Review of Outline rev. 13/14 against experiment-repo fa1ab34. Rev. 13 holds: 55 rows (51 T1, 4 T2), T1 39 no gain / 12 small-undecided, T2 4 of 4 no gain, baseline package 42 / unclipped 13, baseline_valid = 0 in 26 rows, 5 of 13 reference-n rows (alphafold T1 and T2, census_income T1 and T2, forest T1). Alphafold T2 is 1.0043 [1.0039, 1.0047] vs the package; with the baseline undercovering (0.9385) it takes the ‡ mark, as the Outline says.
  > 
  > One wording point on rev. 14 (finite-pool account), nothing else:
  > 
  > The Outline says the observed SD ratio is "consistent with the approximation within Monte Carlo error (about ±0.02 on an SD ratio) at n ≥ 300". In `finite_pop_check.csv` the observed minus predicted sd_ratio at n ≥ 300 is: galaxies 300 −0.009, 500 −0.027, 1000 −0.021, 3000 −0.002; gene_expression 300 −0.023, 500 +0.031, 1000 +0.041, 3000 +0.020; census_income (prediction ≈ 1) 300 −0.035, 500 +0.007, 1000 +0.027, 3000 +0.009. So 5 of 12 differences exceed 0.025 and the largest is 0.041. If ±0.02 is one standard error, the sentence is too strong as written; if it is a band, it is exceeded. The census_income rows, where there is nothing to predict, scatter by up to 0.035, which shows the noise is about that size, so the data support the pattern, not a per-cell fit.
  > 
  > Suggested sentence: "the SD ratio falls with M/P as the approximation predicts (galaxies n = 3000: 0.828 vs 0.831; ratio below 1 in all galaxies cells at n ≥ 300), with differences from the approximation up to 0.04, the size of the scatter in census_income where no effect is predicted". gene_expression n = 500 and 1000 sit above the approximation (0.994 vs 0.964; 0.987 vs 0.946), so the approximation is not quantitative there; say so rather than "quantitatively consistent". The conclusion (overcoverage is a finite-pool effect, not a validity failure of the arm) is unchanged. No reply needed.
